sources.title: git-config Documentation (FILES, --show-origin, --global, --local, Conditional includes)
sources.body: FILES: By default, git config will read configuration options from multiple files: $(prefix)/etc/gitconfig (System-wide configuration file); $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config and ~/.gitconfig (User-specific configuration files. When the XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable is not set or empty, $HOME/.config/ is used as $XDG_CONFIG_HOME. These are also called "global" configuration files. If both files exist, both files are read in the order given above.); $GIT_DIR/config (Repository specific configuration file); $GIT_DIR/config.worktree (This is optional and is only searched when extensions.worktreeConfig is present in $GIT_DIR/config). The files are read in the order given above, with last value found taking precedence over values read earlier. When multiple values are taken then all values of a key from all files will be used. By default, options are only written to the repository specific configuration file. git config will only ever change one file at a time. --show-origin: Augment the output of all queried config options with the origin type (file, standard input, blob, command line) and the actual origin (config file path, ref, or blob id if applicable). --global: For writing options: write to global ~/.gitconfig file rather than the repository .git/config, write to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config file if this file exists and the ~/.gitconfig file doesn't. For reading options: read only from global ~/.gitconfig and from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config rather than from all available files. --local: For writing options: write to the repository .git/config file. This is the default behavior. For reading options: read only from the repository .git/config rather than from all available files. Conditional includes: You can conditionally include a config file from another by setting an includeIf.<condition>.path variable to the name of the file to be included. gitdir: The data that follows the keyword gitdir and a colon is used as a glob pattern. If the location of the .git directory matches the pattern, the include condition is met. If the pattern starts with ~/, ~ will be substituted with the content of the environment variable HOME. If the pattern ends with /, ** will be automatically added (foo/ becomes foo/**). Example: [includeIf "gitdir:~/to/group/"] path = /path/to/foo.inc  -> include for all repositories inside $HOME/to/group. user.name/user.email: The user.name and user.email variables determine what ends up in the author and committer fields of commit objects. If you need the author or committer to be different, the author.name, author.email, committer.name, or committer.email variables can be set. All of these can be overridden by the GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, and EMAIL environment variables. user.useConfigOnly: Instruct Git to avoid trying to guess defaults for user.email and user.name, and instead retrieve the values only from the configuration. For example, if you have multiple email addresses and would like to use a different one for each repository, then with this configuration option set to true in the global config along with a name, Git will prompt you to set up an email before making new commits in a newly cloned repository. Defaults to false.
facts: 설정 파일 읽는 순서: $(prefix)/etc/gitconfig(system) -> $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config 와 ~/.gitconfig(global) -> $GIT_DIR/config(repository) -> $GIT_DIR/config.worktree. 'last value found taking precedence' 이므로 뒤에 읽는 쪽이 이긴다 (system < global < local < worktree).
$GIT_DIR/config.worktree 는 optional 이며 extensions.worktreeConfig 가 $GIT_DIR/config 에 있을 때만 검색된다.
XDG_CONFIG_HOME 이 없거나 비어 있으면 $HOME/.config/ 를 쓴다. global 파일 2개(XDG, ~/.gitconfig)가 둘 다 있으면 둘 다 읽는다.
git config 는 기본적으로 repository 전용 파일(.git/config)에만 쓴다 (--local 이 기본). 한 번에 한 파일만 바꾼다.
--global 쓰기: ~/.gitconfig 에 쓰되, ~/.gitconfig 는 없고 $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config 가 있으면 그쪽에 쓴다. --global 읽기: 모든 파일이 아니라 global 파일에서만 읽는다. --local 읽기도 .git/config 에서만 읽는다.
--show-origin 은 각 설정 값 옆에 origin 종류(file, standard input, blob, command line)와 실제 경로/ref/blob id 를 붙여 준다.

includeIf.<condition>.path 로 조건부 include. gitdir: 조건은 glob 패턴이고 .git 디렉터리 위치가 매치되면 적용. ~/ 로 시작하면 HOME 으로 치환, 끝이 / 이면 ** 자동 추가(foo/ -> foo/**). 예: [includeIf "gitdir:~/to/group/"] path = /path/to/foo.inc
user.name / user.email 은 커밋 객체의 author 와 committer 필드를 결정한다. author.*/committer.* 로 따로 지정 가능하고, 환경변수 GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL, EMAIL 이 이 모두를 덮어쓴다.
user.useConfigOnly=true 를 global 에 두면(이름도 global 에 설정) 새로 clone 한 저장소에서 커밋 전에 git 이 이메일 설정을 요구한다 (기본값 false) — 저장소마다 다른 이메일을 쓰는 경우 용도.

sources.title: Pro Git 1.6 Getting Started - First-Time Git Setup
sources.body: Configuration levels: 1. [path]/etc/gitconfig file: Contains values applied to every user on the system and all their repositories. If you pass the option --system to git config, it reads and writes from this file specifically. Because this is a system configuration file, you would need administrative or superuser privilege to make changes to it. 2. ~/.gitconfig or ~/.config/git/config file: Values specific personally to you, the user. You can make Git read and write to this file specifically by passing the --global option, and this affects all of the repositories you work with on your system. 3. config file in the Git directory (that is, .git/config) of whatever repository you're currently using: Specific to that single repository. You can force Git to read from and write to this file with the --local option, but that is in fact the default. Each level overrides values in the previous level, so values in .git/config trump those in [path]/etc/gitconfig. On Windows systems, Git looks for the .gitconfig file in the $HOME directory (C:\Users\$USER for most people). Your Identity: The first thing you should do when you install Git is to set your user name and email address. This is important because every Git commit uses this information, and it's immutably baked into the commits you start creating: $ git config --global user.name "John Doe"  $ git config --global user.email johndoe@example.com. Again, you need to do this only once if you pass the --global option, because then Git will always use that information for your user on that system. If you want to override this with a different name or email address for specific projects, you can run the command without the --global option when you're in that project. Checking Your Settings: You can view all of your settings and where they are coming from using: $ git config --list --show-origin. To find the origin of one value: $ git config --show-origin rerere.autoUpdate -> file:/home/johndoe/.gitconfig false
facts: 설정 레벨 3단계: --system([path]/etc/gitconfig, 관리자 권한 필요), --global(~/.gitconfig 또는 ~/.config/git/config), --local(.git/config, 기본값). 'Each level overrides values in the previous level' — .git/config 가 system 보다 우선.
Windows 에서는 $HOME 디렉터리(대부분 C:\Users\$USER)에서 .gitconfig 를 찾는다.
책 원문: user.name/user.email 은 'every Git commit uses this information, and it's immutably baked into the commits' — 커밋에 박혀 사후에 바뀌지 않는다.
책 원문 명령: git config --global user.name "John Doe" / git config --global user.email johndoe@example.com. 특정 프로젝트만 다르게 하려면 그 프로젝트 안에서 --global 없이 실행.
git config --list --show-origin 으로 모든 설정과 출처 파일을 본다. 한 키만: git config --show-origin <key> -> 'file:/home/johndoe/.gitconfig<TAB>false' 형태로 최종 값을 정한 파일을 알려준다.

sources.title: git-commit Documentation (--amend, --reset-author, --author, COMMIT INFORMATION)
sources.body: --amend: Replace the tip of the current branch by creating a new commit. The recorded tree is prepared as usual (including the effect of the -i and -o options and explicit pathspec), and the message from the original commit is used as the starting point, instead of an empty message, when no other message is specified from the command line via options such as -m, -F, -c, etc. The new commit has the same parents and author as the current one (the --reset-author option can countermand this). It is a rough equivalent for: git reset --soft HEAD^ ; ... do something else to come up with the right tree ... ; git commit -c ORIG_HEAD but can be used to amend a merge commit. --reset-author: When used with -C/-c/--amend options, or when committing after a conflicting cherry-pick, declare that the authorship of the resulting commit now belongs to the committer. This also renews the author timestamp. --author: Override the commit author. Specify an explicit author using the standard A U Thor <author@example.com> format. Otherwise <author> is assumed to be a pattern and is used to search for an existing commit by that author (i.e. git rev-list --all -i --author=<author>); the commit author is then copied from the first such commit found. COMMIT INFORMATION: Author and committer information is taken from the following environment variables, if set: GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE. In case (some of) these environment variables are not set, the information is taken from the configuration items user.name and user.email, or, if not present, the environment variable EMAIL, or, if that is not set, system user name and the hostname used for outgoing mail (taken from /etc/mailname and falling back to the fully qualified hostname when that file does not exist). The author.name and committer.name and their corresponding email options override user.name and user.email if set and are overridden themselves by the environment variables. The typical usage is to set just the user.name and user.email variables; the other options are provided for more complex use cases.
facts: --amend 는 새 커밋을 만들어 현재 브랜치의 tip 을 교체한다. 새 커밋은 기존 커밋과 같은 parents 와 author 를 가진다 — 'the --reset-author option can countermand this'. 즉 amend 만 하면 작성자는 안 바뀌고, --reset-author 를 함께 써야 바뀐다.
--reset-author: -C/-c/--amend 와 함께 쓸 때(또는 충돌 난 cherry-pick 뒤 커밋할 때) 결과 커밋의 authorship 을 committer(=현재 설정의 사용자)로 선언하며 author timestamp 도 갱신한다.
--author="A U Thor <author@example.com>" 로 이번 커밋의 author 만 명시 지정 가능. 이 형식이 아니면 패턴으로 간주해 기존 커밋에서 검색(git rev-list --all -i --author=<author>)하고 처음 찾은 커밋의 author 를 복사한다.

author/committer 결정 우선순위: 환경변수 GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* -> author.*/committer.* 설정 -> user.name/user.email -> EMAIL 환경변수 -> 시스템 사용자명+호스트명. author.name/committer.name 은 user.* 를 덮어쓰고 환경변수가 그것을 덮어쓴다.
문서 원문: 'The typical usage is to set just the user.name and user.email variables'. 이름은 관례상 사람 이름이지만 Git 이 형식을 강제하지 않고, 인증(authentication)과는 무관하다 (인증은 credential.username).

sources.title: GitHub Docs - Setting your commit email address
sources.body: GitHub Docs page on choosing the email address associated with commits. For web-based Git operations the setting is under email settings: 'Keep my email addresses private'. For commits made from the command line, the page gives the commands: global setup 'git config --global user.email "YOUR_EMAIL"' and single repository setup 'git config user.email "YOUR_EMAIL"' (run inside the repository, without --global). The page references the GitHub-provided noreply email address and says 'For more information about the exact form the no-reply email address can take, see Email addresses reference' (linked). The page also states that any commits made prior to changing your commit email address are still associated with your previous email address ('Any commits you made prior to changing your commit email address are still associated with your previous email address'). Because changing git config only affects new commits, past commits keep the old address unless history is rewritten.
facts: GitHub Docs 명령: 전역 `git config --global user.email "YOUR_EMAIL"`, 단일 저장소 `git config user.email "YOUR_EMAIL"` (해당 저장소 안에서 --global 없이).
원문: 이메일을 바꾸기 전에 만든 커밋은 여전히 이전 이메일과 연결된 채로 남는다 ('still associated with your previous email address').
웹 기반 Git 작업용 설정 항목명은 'Keep my email addresses private' (이메일 설정 화면).

sources.title: GitHub Docs - Email addresses reference
sources.body: GitHub Docs reference for email address types. Noreply address formats quoted from the page: 'ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com' and 'USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com'. The page references the cutoff date July 18, 2017: accounts created after that date get an ID-based noreply address (ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com); accounts created before it get a username-based address (USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com), provided 'Keep my email address private' was enabled before that date. You can select (or deselect and reselect) 'Keep my email address private' in your email settings to get an ID-based noreply address. The phrase 'Block command line pushes' did not appear in the fetched content of this page.
facts: noreply 주소 형식 두 가지: ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com (ID 기반), USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com (사용자명 기반).
2017-07-18 이후 생성된 계정은 ID 기반 noreply 주소를 받는다. 그 이전 계정은 그 날짜 전에 'Keep my email address private' 를 켠 경우에만 USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com 형태.
이메일 설정에서 'Keep my email address private' 를 선택(또는 껐다가 다시 켬)하면 ID 기반 noreply 주소를 받을 수 있다.

sources.title: Pro Git 7.6 Git Tools - Rewriting History
sources.body: Changing Multiple Commit Messages: to modify a commit farther back, use git rebase -i with the parent of the last commit you want to edit (e.g. git rebase -i HEAD~3); change 'pick' to 'edit' for each commit to stop at, then git rebase --continue. 'Remember again that this is a rebasing command - every commit in the range HEAD~3..HEAD with a changed message and all of its descendants will be rewritten. Don't include any commit you've already pushed to a central server - doing so will confuse other developers by providing an alternate version of the same change.' Changing Email Addresses Globally: 'Another common case is that you forgot to run git config to set your name and email address before you started working ... you can change email addresses in multiple commits in a batch with filter-branch as well. You need to be careful to change only the email addresses that are yours, so you use --commit-filter' (example with GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL / GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and git commit-tree). 'Because commits contain the SHA-1 values of their parents, this command changes every commit SHA-1 in your history, not just those that have the matching email address.' Caution on the page: 'git filter-branch has many pitfalls, and is no longer the recommended way to rewrite history. Instead, consider using git-filter-repo'. On changing the last commit: 'You need to be careful with this technique because amending changes the SHA-1 of the commit. It's like a very small rebase - don't amend your last commit if you've already pushed it.'
facts: 책 원문: amend 는 커밋의 SHA-1 을 바꾼다 — 이미 push 한 마지막 커밋은 amend 하지 말 것.
git rebase -i HEAD~3 처럼 범위를 지정해 'pick' 을 'edit' 로 바꾸고 git rebase --continue 로 과거 커밋을 수정. 범위 내 변경 커밋과 그 후손 전부가 다시 쓰이므로 이미 중앙 서버에 push 한 커밋은 포함하지 말 것.
책이 'git config 를 먼저 안 하고 작업 시작' 을 흔한 사례로 들고 filter-branch --commit-filter 로 이메일을 일괄 교체하는 예를 보여줌. 이 방식은 히스토리의 모든 커밋 SHA-1 을 바꾼다.
책 경고 원문: git filter-branch 는 함정이 많아 더 이상 권장되지 않으며 git-filter-repo 를 고려하라.

conflicts.about: git config 레벨 수 / global 파일 위치
conflicts.a: Pro Git 책: system / global / local 3단계, global 은 '~/.gitconfig or ~/.config/git/config'
conflicts.b: git-config 문서 FILES: system / global(XDG + ~/.gitconfig 둘 다 읽음) / repository / worktree 4종 파일. 책에는 worktree 레벨이 없음 (충돌이라기보다 책이 덜 자세함)

unknowns: GitHub 'Block command line pushes that expose my email' 설정: 가져온 GitHub Docs 두 페이지 본문에 해당 문구가 없었다 (다른 페이지 미조회).
git rebase --exec 'git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit' 로 여러 커밋 작성자를 일괄 변경하는 공식 문서 근거: 이번에 git-rebase 문서를 읽지 않아 미확인.
includeIf 를 이용한 회사/개인 이메일 분리의 구체 예시(hasconfig:remote.*.url 등)와 includeIf 적용 여부를 --show-origin 으로 확인하는 동작: git-config 문서는 gitdir 예시만 읽었고 실측하지 않음.
git config user.name 미설정 시 커밋 에러 메시지 원문('Please tell me who you are' 등): 1차 자료 미확인.
각 페이지의 발행/수정일: 페이지에 표시되지 않아 publishedAt 모두 null.
